newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Branson's Virgin Express may seek bourse listing.
newsitem.headline: Branson's Virgin Express may seek bourse listing.

text.p: Richard Branson's fledgling Virgin Express regional airline has performed well above par in 1996 and said on Tuesday that future plans might include a bourse listing.
"There's no question that (a bourse listing) is an alternative," Virgin Express's chief executive officer Jonathan Ornstein told Reuters by telephone.
But he added that the Brussels-based carrier, which was launched in April 1996 after Branson bought 90 percent of EuroBelgian Airlines (EBA), was in no hurry to float its stock.
"Quite frankly, business is going very well and we're not in a huge rush to make a decision one way or the other," he said.
"There are a lot of different alternatives. Let's put it like this, every investment banker on the street has come and talked to us," he said.
One of the alternatives would also be to do nothing, he said. "We're a nice private company and I tell you there are some really nice advantages to being private," he said.
A Virgin Express listing would follow in the wake of a similar move by Ireland's "low-fares no-frills" airline Ryanair Holdings Plc, which is run by U.S. entrepreneur David Bonderman.
Ryanair made its debut on the Nasdaq and Irish stock exchanges on May 29.
Ornstein said that Virgin Express had so far been focusing on running its day-to-day business instead of pondering its future.
"The bigger picture items have sort of been put on to the backburner a little bit," he said.
Ornstein added he had not been considering whether to list in Brussels or on Nasdaq but declined to say whether a prospectus was already being worked on.
He added that apparently "the U.S. market at least seems to be hungry for airlines that might take advantage of deregulation".
He was unable to say when the company would finally decide whether to list Virgin Express.
"Working at Virgin, there could even be a decision tomorrow," he said.
Ornstein said that the first five months of 1997 showed that Virgin Express's growth had clearly exceeded all expectations.
"Our growth this year will be in excess of 40 percent in turnover," he said. The company had a turnover of about $200 million last year.

Virgin Express has already signed codeshare deals with Belgian flag carrier Sabena, which is owned 49.5 percent by Swissair, for flights between Brussels and London Heathrow, London Gatwick, Rome and Barcelona.
Ornstein said Virgin Express was working on new deals but declined to give details.
"This is Virgin, there's always deals in the pipeline, always things that we talk about, but nothing is imminent," he said.
